data.narrative:
HEO, a Series A space & aerospace company founded by Dr. Will Crowe and Dr. Hiranya Jayakody, has raised $12M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a universe of 14 same-sector peers: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using total capital raised ($12M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent funding, this method implies a $24M valuation. Peer-median triangulation could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within tight valuation bands; while 14 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets yielded three or more datapoints. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (sector median 27.4x across the five public tickers) is inapplicable without the target's revenue, which private companies typically do not disclose.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20M to $28M, centered on $24M. This range carries meaningful uncertainty given reliance on a single triangulation method and the lack of narrowly comparable private peers at the same stage and scale. Revenue disclosure or revenue-based comps would substantially strengthen conviction. Key risks include stage-progression volatility and the target's specific operational metrics relative to the broader space sector cohort.
